metadata.scenario_context: Emily is ill, and Mike and Kim will visit Emily in the hospital.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to hospital visit.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of flowers to bring to Emily’s hospital visit.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, do you think we should bring some chrysanthemums for Emily? I heard they are her favorite flowers. 

Also, um... do you think it’s worth considering if we should, you know, maybe... pay the doctors a little extra for better service? Just a thought...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums sound like a great choice, especially if they're her favorite. We should definitely get those. 

As for paying extra to the doctors... I really don’t think that’s necessary. In Taiwan ROC, we believe in getting proper service without having to resort to bribery. It’s just not how things should work, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective, but... I can't help but think that sometimes it’s just how things operate. In China, paying a little extra can sometimes really help with getting better care, you know? It’s not ideal, but... it seems to be a common practice. Just wondering if it might be something to consider...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I get what you're saying, and I can see how things might work differently in China. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, like wanting the best care for our loved ones. I think there are always ways to communicate and get things done without resorting to extra payments. We both know, at the end of the day, it's about trust and respect in the healthcare system. So let's focus on making Emily feel better with those chrysanthemums!
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
